To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the functional organization of early visual cortex is modulated in a task-dependent manner, and that this modulation is reflected in changes in the sensitivity and connectivity patterns of subpopulations within early visual areas.
1. Feature-specific attention alters the sensitivity of neuronal subpopulates within individual early visual regions.
attention alters the functional connectivity of visual cortical areas, without changing the univariate responses of the same areas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the brain represents the world.
how the brain responds to visual information.
the way in which the human brain represents the visual world, and the way in which this representation is modulated by top down attentional mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the visual cortex is not a static structure but a dynamic system, which is constantly adapting to the task demands and the visual environment.
feature specific attentional modulation is a property of the functional organization of the cortex, not of its response properties.
feature specific modulation of visual areas is a complex phenomenon, which depends on both the bottom up stimulus and the task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
attentional tasks alter the way that early visual areas communicate with each others, but that this does not necessarily lead to changes in their univariate responses.
attention is a process that alters the functional architecture of visual cortex, not its overall activity.
attentional modulation of visual areas is driven by the recruitment of specific sub-populations within each area.
The main takeaway from our work is that
attentional modulation of the visual cortex is not a simple process but rather is complex and feature specific.
the functional architecture of visual cortex is highly sensitive to task demands, even in the absence of a change in stimulus.

the functional architecture of visual cortex is highly flexible and that the spatial scale at and the mechanisms by which attention alters neural activity depend on the nature of the task and the stimulus.
